If it is an issue, you raise it in an appropriate way, but not in court. So far as the first matter is concerned, then I've already indicated to you that if you can justify re-calling the witness, then that will be allowed and we will address the issue as and when it's raised with us and the OTP have a chance to reply to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the second matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I note that in the course of that cross-examination, when the witness asked if you would like to know where he had driven, Mr. Lukic, you said you would come back to that. Are you not intending to come back to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked about the phone calls but I forgot that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to continue. I do apologise, Mr. Protic. You say that in the period when Obrad Stevanovic was at the head of the staff in Kosovo you sometimes drove Sreten Lukic around. Can you tell us where, if you can remember; when, if you can remember that; and with whom, if you can remember.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Sreten Lukic, Mirko Bozic, and Savo Mastorevic from -- I drove these people to Gnjilane from the staff in Pristina. They took with them decisions on the dismissal of employees of Albanian ethnicity. 70 such documents which they took to the station in Gnjilane, and they threw the people out on the street. I remember that as if it was yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that we're talking about this, did the Albanians boycott and leave the police due to pressure from their Albanian community?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether they left, but they were given decisions on dismissal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can one be dismissed if one fails to report to work for three days in a row?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Well, you should ask the personnel people that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You should know.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Well, I always carried out all my tasks and was never late for work.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that anyone was dismissed from the police because he failed to turn up for work for three or five days in a row.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we just look at what you just said. You said, in respect to what happened in Gnjilane, Mr. Lukic, Mr. Bozic, Mr. Mastorevic took me -- them -- decisions under dismissal of employees of Albanian ethnicity. 70 such documents which they took to the station in Gnjilane and they threw the people down the street. I remember that as if it was yesterday. Just tell us exactly what you personally observed at Gnjilane, what you saw happen.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: The lists were made in the staff in Pristina, the documents were typed out, they were taken to Gnjilane, and they were handed to the employees of the secretariat in Gnjilane.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Who handed them?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Savo Mastorevic spoke Albanian well. He read them out in Albanian and he handed them to the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember when this was? Approximately if you can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: In the period of the 23rd of -- 23rd to the -- of April to the 31st of July, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Earlier on in answer to a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move from that. Are you saying this happened on one occasion only, in that period of time, or are you saying it happened on more than one occasion as many.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said Mr. Lukic offered you a vacant flat which had in it a policeman who was an invalid. When did this happened? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Just before I was pensioned off.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About how long before? If you can't be precise, just give us an approximation.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: A month or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In what circumstances did you come to be speaking with Mr. Lukic at that time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: I was looking for a flat because I couldn't bear living in Batajnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm asking you what circumstances in which you came to speak to Mr. Lukic at that time.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: I went to see him. I asked him to receive me, through his secretary; I went into his office and I asked him for a flat. He said that Djukaric Kapadina [phoen], there's a flat. Go and take a look at it with your wife. If you like it, move in. I went there and I saw it was inhabited by a policeman, an invalid with three children who had moved in illegally. But I didn't want to do that so I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You also said much later on in cross-examination that you offered General Lukic to take your apartment in Batajnica. Was this the same occasion or was it a different occasion?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: In that period when I was looking for a flat, I was offering my flat to the ministry so that they could give it to someone who had nothing to do with Batajnica, to a police employee in Batajnica or somewhere else. And in exchange, I wanted a place in Belgrade which was far from Batajnica and those graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Well, may I put the question this way then. How many times did you meet with Mr. Lukic in respect to your housing situation, in respect to the flat?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Four or five times. In the end he told me, "Why do you keep bothering me?" "I do insist."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said you went to see General Lukic and General Djordjevic also came to Bujanovac. Could you explain a little bit? When General Djordjevic came to Bujanovac and you saw Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Mistake, mistake. Error. There's an error in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what happened when you went to see Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: I was in Mr. Lukic's office. Mr. Djordjevic came in to the office in Belgrade, and they discussed it with me and we all agreed that I should go to Bujanovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: About when did this occur?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: It happened when the refrigerator truck emerged and when the media started reporting about the transport of corpses from Kosovo to Serbia, when it became public.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: During -- I think I'll move on. You said to me earlier on today that you would drive Mr. Lukic from time to time in the 1990s and it seemed that in -- it seemed that you said in answer to my friend just now that you drove him only in a period during the year 1990. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: No, no. You misunderstand me. When I was sent there, according to the decision, and drove Obrad Stevanovic, I also drove General Lukic, who only came from time to time. He had his own driver in Belgrade but he went down there. Sometimes he would come with a driver, sometimes without. When he arrived without a driver, I was at his disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What I want to find out from you is whether or not you drove him only in the year 1990, or did you drive him at all during the years of the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Asked and answered, Your Honour. I specifically asked this question several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think there is a certain amount of doubt, and it would help us to have it clarified so we'll allow the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you follow the question or would you like me to repeat it? Can you tell us whether or not you drove Mr. Lukic only in the year 1990 or did you drive him during the years of the 1990s?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Sreten Lukic had his own personal driver in Belgrade, who belonged to the cabinet. When Sreten Lukic went out in the field, like the staff commander, he would take his own driver with him. I was not General Lukic's personal driver, officially, on paper, ever, but I would drive him around if he arrived in Kosovo without his driver or if his driver brought him there and then went back. I was at the disposal of the staff commander; I followed his orders. And if he told me to drive someone somewhere, I would do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Protic, we understand that. The question is about the period over which this happened. Did it only happen in 1990 or did it happen also in later years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had never driven Mr. Lukic privately or officially --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Protic, we know that you were not his driver. We know you didn't -- that he had his own driver and that it was only on occasions when he arrived without a driver that you were at his disposal; that is clear. What we want to know is over what period of time that situation occasionally happened. Was it only in the three months and four months in 1990 or did it happen in other years as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only during the period that was already mentioned in 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now, apart from driving him --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: I believe the witness said in the 1990s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We -- Mr. Protic, Mr. Protic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You'll need to ask this again, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You don't need the documents, Mr. Protic. We know that you had occasion, without being the official, assigned driver, but you had occasion to drive Mr. Lukic during 1990. Did you have occasion to drive him during any other period, separate and apart from 1990? We understand that situation.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: I understand, I understand. General Lukic, when he came over from Kosovo to Belgrade at a weekend, I would drive him and his belongings to his flat, and this may have happened once or twice. It could be regarded as a private matter because it had nothing to do with any official assignments. That was the only time I drove him; never before, never after. Of course, except for the period that I mentioned between the 23rd of April and the 31st of July, and even in that period it was only occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you drove him to his flat, was that in 1990 or was that in some other year?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: That's not important at all. The man would come from the field --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Protic, we will decide what's important. Please answer the question that you're being asked. Tell us when this was. It's a simple matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you let us know, please, when it was you took him to his flat?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Well, let the answer then be: In the 1990s. Not 1990, but the 1990s.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: And for how many years? For how long? How many years you have been doing this duty? In 1990? For how many years? Can you count the years? One, two, three, four, five, how many years you have been doing it? In what period? That's the question. Even in 1990, because 1990 that would mean about nine years. How much of time? One, two, three, count that. How many years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I drove him only twice with his belongings when he would come from his field work. I don't know whether he came from Kosovo or from elsewhere, but I was an official driver from MUP and I would have a travel order, and on that basis I would take General Lukic to his flat, and there's nothing controversial about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: But you spoke of 1990. What do you mean by "1990"? Or 1990s? Explain that, please, because that is causing the confusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1990, in the period between -- in the period between 23rd April and 31st July, I was an assigned driver. In that period I drove Mr. Lukic whenever he came to Pristina on business. I would drive him there and drive him back. I wasn't his personal driver; I was just a driver at his disposal. This is valid for the period I mentioned. The gentleman asked me whether I drove him on some other occasions. From 1990 up until my retirement, I drove him twice throughout that period, and that's the long and the short of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Protic, you worked in the MUP during the course of the period, the 1990s. Apart from driving Mr. Lukic, in that period, did you have opportunity to speak with him or he to speak with you at any time in any circumstances?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose to him. These were conversations of no consequence. This was nothing official. I didn't have any dealings with the staff as far as some decisions were concerned. I was a driver. Whoever got in the car with me, I would discuss private matters with him. I didn't make any decisions, nor was this part of my job, to join any conversations or give any advice or anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that it was part of your job. But you spoke with him -- you had opportunity to speak with him unofficially. Where would you have these opportunities to speak with him unofficially in that period?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR PROTIC
utterances.text: In the car, and never about business.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Let me ask the question again. Forget about the car. I'm not asking you anything about driving a car --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Specific question, specific answer; there is nothing else to be clarified. When did you speak? In the car. How many times you drive him? Two times. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Those weren't the questions that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree. The matter has been dealt with. Let's move on to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That was the last subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Protic, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give evidence, and you're now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, is there anything to report on the question I asked Mr. Hannis this morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I know up until lunchtime - and that's just about an hour and a half ago - there was nothing. And I suspect that there -- nothing has borne fruit as yet. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As far as next week's witness list is concerned, am I right in noting that there are only two witnesses planned?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Two witnesses confirmed -- two witnesses confirmed; however, we may -- should be able to bring on another one pending a decision which we are seeking from the Chamber. That's K82.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, as matters stand at the moment, we are scheduled to have sittings on Monday and Tuesday of next week from 9.00 to 3.30, and it is our intention to adhere to that schedule, if possible. The other three days of next week in the afternoon another case will occupy this courtroom, and therefore we will be confined to sitting from 9.00 to 1.45. So we now adjourn until Monday --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it is important and there might be some information in respect to the question that was asked, perhaps we could convey to the Court and to the other parties --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- there is nothing I could usefully add at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall adjourn now until Monday at 9.00.
